A **cubit** was a unit of measurement corresponding to the distance between an average person’s elbow and middle fingertip, or about 46 centimeters or 18 inches. A **handbreadth** was a unit of measurement equal to the width of a person’s hand, or about 8 centimeters or 3 inches. The **cubits** used here were long cubits, each equal to a regular cubit plus a handbreadth, or about 54 centimeters or 21 inches. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could express these measurements in modern measurements, either in the text or a footnote. Alternate translation: [in long cubits, each of which is about 54 centimeters or 21 inches]

A **bosom** here is a gutter or trench that went around the base of the altar. If your readers would not be familiar with what this is, you could use the name of a similar thing that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [and a trench]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if the outer edge of the gutter were a **lip**. It means that the gutter had a raised rim around its outer edge. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and its border to its raised outer edge]

14.note: This could mean: (1) that the measurement begins at the bottom of the **bosom**, which is cut into the **ground**. Alternate translation: [And from the ground at the bottom of the bosom] (2) that the measurement begins at the **ground** at the edge of the **bosom**. Alternate translation: [And from the ground at the edge of the bosom]

A **setback** here is a ledge around the altar where each higher section of the altar became narrower than the section below it. If your readers would not be familiar with what this is, you could use the name of a similar thing that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [the lower ledge or setback]

15.note: This could mean: (1) that the **hearth** is **four cubits** above the “great setback” in the previous verse. This would make the altar 10 cubits high. Alternate translation: [And the hearth is four cubits above the great setback] (2) that the **hearth** is **four cubits** above the “small setback” in the previous verse. This means that the **hearth** rests immediately on top of the “great setback.” This would make the altar 6 cubits high. Alternate translation: [And the hearth is four cubits above the lower setback]

A **hearth** is a place where a fire is burned. Here it refers to the top section of the altar, where the priests burned the sacrifices. The original language uses two slightly different words for this part in this verse, but they both seem to refer to the same thing. If your readers would not be familiar with what a hearth is, you could use the name of a similar thing that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [And the hearth, the place on top of the altar for burning sacrifices, is four cubits]

Alternate translation: [and the priests shall throw salt on them to show that the offerings are pure and that Yahweh’s covenant with his people will last]

25.note: Yahweh is using **do** as a common expression of the culture to mean “offer.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [you shall offer a male goat for a sin offering]

25.q: וּ⁠פַ֧ר בֶּן בָּקָ֛ר וְ⁠אַ֥יִל מִן הַ⁠צֹּ֖אן תְּמִימִ֥ים יַעֲשֽׂוּ
25.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about what the priests **shall do** before the information about the animals that they were to offer. Alternate translation: [and they shall do a bull, a son of cattle, and a ram from the flock, perfect]
See how you translated the similar expression in 43:19.

26.note: Yahweh is using **fill its hand** as a common expression of the culture to mean “dedicate it for service to God.” This could mean: (1) the priests will dedicate the altar to Yahweh, as the ULT shows. (2) the priests themselves will be ordained for their service, as some ancient manuscripts and versions read “their hand.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and they shall set it apart for serving me]

27.q: אֶת עוֹלֽוֹתֵי⁠כֶם֙ וְ⁠אֶת שַׁלְמֵי⁠כֶ֔ם וְ⁠רָצִ֣אתִי אֶתְ⁠כֶ֔ם
27.note: The words **your** and **you** are plural here because Yahweh is addressing the Israelites, so use the plural form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.
See how you translated the similar expression in 5:11.
